_comment: Prompts for TOP-ONLY ground tiles (tiles/pipeline/tops.py). These sheets are judged on the top surface alone: the wall and the overhang are never shown, so nothing here asks for a transition, an edge, a tuft or a spill. (Maintainer brief 2026-08-27: 'the wall and overhang is 100% unimportant'.) NEVER reuse these prompts for the x-over-y matrix, and never offer a sheet generated from them as an x-over-y candidate.
_prompt_comment: Two flavours per ground, one axis between them: DENSITY. 'subtle' is a base-tile-set member, so it says quiet/even/little variation; 'detail' is a once-in-a-while tile, so it says rich/varied/lots of detail. Short keyword prompts, no named features (PixelLab invents flowers, cracks and bubbles unasked on a plain ground prompt, so naming one spends prompt weight on something that arrives for free). Colour is named in WORDS and aimed at config/palette.json's `top` for that ground - no #hex here, unlike config/tiles.json flat_base, because a textured top must keep its own variation and hex-anchoring flattens it.

flavours.subtle: repeat-safe base texture - a field of it must not show where the repeat starts
flavours.detail: a showpiece tile placed once in a while, never tiled across an area

black_rock.detail: black volcanic rock, deep black, glassy sharp glints, bold sparse forms, rich detail

brown_paving_stone.detail: beautiful old brown paving, warm grey brown, richly worn and varied, lots of detail

dark_mud.detail: churned wet mud, deep cold brown, glossy sheen, coarse and uneven, lots of detail

deep_water.detail: beautiful deep sea, dark navy, slow heavy swell, moonlit shimmer, rich detail

grass.detail: beautiful meadow grass, deep green, sunlit, rich and varied, lots of detail

_why_comment: Why each prompt reads the way it does, kept so the choice is not re-litigated. 'set 1/2/3' are the three competing proposal sets from the 2026-08-27 prompt round; criterion 2 = name no feature the generator supplies unasked, criterion 5 = the words must separate this ground from its neighbours (water/deep_water, light_soil/light_beach).

black_rock.subtle: Set 3, trimmed 'ground' to 'rock' for material clarity — it is the only set whose colour word ('near black') actually matches palette #1e1d1e, and it names nothing but grain.
black_rock.detail: Rewrite on set 3's spine: set 1's 'obsidian veins/fractures' and set 2's colourless prompt both failed criteria 2 and 5, so I kept the glassy-glint keyword, added set 2's sparse/bold scale knob, and dropped every named feature.

brown_paving_stone.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — 'warm grey brown' is the single most palette-accurate colour phrase in any set (#7d7265 is a grey-brown, not a brown), and 'evenly laid, worn smooth, plain' is pure density language.
brown_paving_stone.detail: Set 3 with its weak colour word ('warm stone') replaced by the subtle slot's 'warm grey brown'; set 1's 'deep shadowed joints, varied blocks' named features the generator supplies unasked.

dark_mud.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — shortest of the three, 'cold brown' matches #514137, and 'almost featureless' is the strongest repeat-safe density cue offered.
dark_mud.detail: Set 3 plus set 2's grain knob ('coarse and uneven'); set 1's 'sparse deep pits' named a feature and set 2 alone carried no colour at all.

deep_water.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — 'still deep sea' is the only phrasing that separates this ground from `water` on the noun rather than on an adjective, which criterion 5 demands.
deep_water.detail: Set 3 verbatim — 'slow heavy swell, moonlit shimmer' is motion and light, not named objects, and it keeps the dark navy that #162843 asks for; set 1's 'rolling ripples, scattered reflections' drifts toward shallow water.

grass.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — 'deep green' is the only colour phrase pointed at #14523b's pine rather than PixelLab's default yellow-green, and set 1's 'fine even blades' names blades.
grass.detail: Rewrite: set 3's spine with the waffly 'the most beautiful' cut and set 2's light knob ('sunlit') folded in — set 1's 'thick clumped blades, sparse tall growth' names exactly the features the maintainer says arrive for free.

grey_paving_stone.subtle: Set 3 with 'stones' added so the ground reads as paving and not as a grey floor; 'cool pale grey' is right for #a8a8a8 and 'evenly laid, worn flat, plain' carries the density axis.
grey_paving_stone.detail: Set 3 with 'stones' added and 'pale silver stone' tightened to 'pale silver grey' so the colour keyword is a colour; 'finely cut, richly worn' beats set 1's 'crisp shadow joints'.

grey_stone.subtle: Set 3's opening plus set 1's 'fine even grain', with 'plain grey' made 'plain medium grey' to hit #808082 rather than drifting light.
grey_stone.detail: Rewrite: all three were weak here — set 1 named fissures, set 2 named no colour, set 3's 'silver grey' sits too light for #808082 — so I kept craggy/mottled and a single depth word.

ice.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — nine words, no named feature, and 'still/smooth/faint/calm' is unambiguous low-density language.
ice.detail: Rewrite from set 3 with set 2's gloss and translucence keywords: set 1's 'sparse deep cyan fractures, glassy facets' named two features, which criterion 2 forbids.

lava.subtle: Set 1, trimmed and with the colour word promoted to 'bright orange' — set 3's 'cooling / dull deep orange' and set 2's 'mostly dark' both fight palette #fd5a02, which is a hot orange.
lava.detail: Set 3 plus a contrast knob — 'blazing orange and yellow, bright flowing glow' keeps the palette hue, where set 1's 'white-hot veins, dark cooling crust' names features and darkens the tile.

light_beach.subtle: Set 3 with 'beach' restored to the noun so the ground cannot be confused with `light_soil`; 'warm cream' matches #e4c495 and 'fine even grain, undisturbed' is the density cue.
light_beach.detail: Set 3 with 'beach' added and 'pale gold' warmed to 'warm pale gold' for #e4c495; set 1's 'sparse coarse grit, rippled wind texture' was longer for no extra keyword.

light_soil.subtle: Rewrite: criterion 5 decides this slot — set 3's 'pale earth' and set 1's 'fine even dust' both read as sand, so I took set 2's unambiguous 'dry soil' noun and set 3's sentence shape, with 'light warm brown' for #c9ab7e.
light_soil.detail: Set 3's 'freshly turned' opening (the strongest anti-sand keyword in any set), trimmed, with the colour made explicit; set 1's 'crumbly clods, cracked gritty surface, coarse lumps' named three features.

parquet_floor.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — 'even repeating grain' is precisely what a base-set floor tile needs and no set said it better.
parquet_floor.detail: Set 3 rewritten to drop 'old hall', which is a scene word that risks the model inventing surroundings, keeping its 'polished, richly patterned' and correcting 'honey' to 'warm brown' for #a7754b.

slime.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — nine words, and 'green slime' plus 'even smooth sheen' keeps it slime rather than generic goo without naming a bubble.
slime.detail: Set 3 with 'heavy' swapped for 'thick' and gloss made explicit; set 1's 'sparse fat bubbles, bright rim highlights' named the one feature PixelLab reliably invents on its own.

snow.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — 'quiet unbroken snow ... almost no variation' is the cleanest low-density statement of the thirty proposals.
snow.detail: Set 3 plus set 2's 'cold blue shadows', which is both a contrast knob and true to #ebf4f6's blue-white; set 1's 'drifted windswept crust' says the same thing with a feature noun.

water.subtle: Set 3 verbatim — 'calm shallow water' separates it from `deep_water` on the noun, and 'gentle even ripples' is the density cue.
water.detail: Set 3 with 'shallow' added for the same separation and 'bright blue' softened to 'clear blue' for #7eb7c7; set 1's 'sparkling caustics' is a word the model will not weigh.
